subject: zoology
question_text: Name the four extra embryonic membranes.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.56, VSAQ 118). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What they are
steps.margin_note: One or two lines saying what they are, then the list. The names carry the second mark.
lines: Extra embryonic membranes are membranes that
grow out of the embryo but do not become part
They are found in reptiles, birds and mammals,
steps.why: The membranes are named extra embryonic because they lie outside the embryo proper, and that is why they are shed at birth or at hatching.
common_mistakes: Writing that they are organs of the embryo. They are outside the embryo and are left behind.
Giving them to amphibians and fishes. Only reptiles, birds and mammals have them.
steps.memory_tip: Extra means outside: outside the embryo, so they are thrown away at birth.

steps.label: The four names
steps.margin_note: The four names alone can earn the mark; one short use each makes the answer complete.
lines: 1) Amnion holds the amniotic fluid, which
protects the embryo from shock and drying.
2) Chorion is the outermost membrane and helps
3) Allantois stores the nitrogenous waste and
4) Yolk sac holds the yolk, the food of the
steps.why: Each membrane has one job, so learning them as protect, exchange, store, feed keeps all four apart in the exam.
common_mistakes: Naming the placenta as one of the four. The placenta is formed from the chorion and the allantois.
Writing three names only. The question asks for four.
steps.memory_tip: Protect, exchange, store, feed: amnion, chorion, allantois, yolk sac.

insider_note: This is a naming question, so the four words are the answer; the one-line uses are insurance if one name is misspelt.
